title: Twenty Percent Appears, Exits the Next Day—Yet Crude Oil Returns
part1:
Seen as a short drama over two days, this crude oil market story moves very quickly. A major proposal appeared on the first day and was withdrawn the next day. But the market did not leave the stage according to that script.

On July 13, Mr. Trump posted that for all cargo passing through the Strait of Hormuz, the United States would seek payment equal to 20 percent of the cost of providing safety and security.

However, this was not a finished fee system. It did not say who would pay, how the amount would be calculated, or how it would be collected. Its legal basis was also unclear. What appeared on the stage was not the details of the system, but the large number of 20 percent.
part2:
On the same day, Brent crude oil futures rose sharply. The settlement price at the end of trading was $83.30 a barrel. This was an increase of $7.29, or 9.59 percent, from the previous day. Reports linked this rise to concerns about a U.S. blockade of Iran at sea, which was said to begin the next day, and about energy shipments passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

Then, on the next day, July 14, came the first twist. Mr. Trump posted that he was withdrawing the 20 percent payment plan and replacing it with trade and investment deals between the Gulf states and the United States. He also told reporters that no one should charge ships passing through the strait, and that he did not like the idea of charging a fee at all.
part3:
If the plan had disappeared, would crude oil return to its previous level? Here, the market added another twist. After the withdrawal, Brent futures briefly reduced their gains, but soon returned to a high level close to where they had been before the announcement. At the time the article was published, they were up about 2.6 percent and above $85 a barrel. The settlement price that day was also $84.73, up 1.7 percent from the previous day.

In other words, what disappeared was one policy proposal. The concerns about a blockade at sea, attacks between the United States and Iran, and the safety of tankers did not disappear. The market was watching not only what would happen to the statement, but also what would happen to the routes that carry crude oil. The danger around a distant strait does not disappear just because a post is withdrawn. This market showed that fact like a short drama series.
in_one_line: Oil prices stayed high after Trump withdrew a proposed Strait of Hormuz fee because shipping dangers remained.
